messages.author: c584965fac2b99d6
messages.subject: Loading data from https sources
parts:
What's the best way of loading data in to a Shiny app from an https data source (eg u="https://api.scraperwiki.com/api/1.0/datastore/sqlite?format=csv&name=nhs_sit_reps&query=select%20SHA%2CName%2C%20fromDateStr%2CtoDateStr%2C%20tableName%2CfacetB%2Cvalue%20from%20fulltable%20%20where%20Name%20like%20'%25WIGH%25'" )

A recipe I have used in the past is to load the data in this way:

floader=function(fn){
  temporaryFile <- tempfile()
  download.file(fn,destfile=temporaryFile, method="curl")
  read.csv(temporaryFile)
}

However, the demo shiny app I built around this approach - http://glimmer.rstudio.com/psychemedia/wightsitrep/  code here: http://blog.ouseful.info/2012/11/28/quick-shiny-demo-exploring-nhs-winter-sit-rep-data/ ) which was working fine seems to have died a few days ago and started throwing an RWebsocket error?

tony

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: Loading data from https sources
parts:
I don't know for sure, but I doubt the RWebsocket issue is related to the https downloading issue. I think your method of downloading files via https should work, especially if it worked in the past.


I recently made a little package called downloader, which tries to abstract away from the details of using internal/curl/wget when downloading https files.
http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/downloader/index.html

You would use it like this:
library(downloader)
download('https://url.com/file.txt")

Depending on the platform and availability of the different download methods (internal/curl/wget/lynx), it'll try different methods of downloading the file.

-Winston
